categories.main_business_segments: Henan Shijia Photons Technology Co., Ltd. primarily operates in three main business segments: optical chips and devices, indoor optical cables, and cable materials. Their product portfolio includes PLC planar lightwave circuit splitter chips, AWG arrayed waveguide grating chips, DFB laser chips, optical fiber connectors, indoor optical cables, and cable materials. These products serve applications in backbone networks, metropolitan area networks, fiber-to-the-home (FTTH), data centers, and 5G infrastructure.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company employs an Integrated Device Manufacturer (IDM) model covering chip design, wafer fabrication, chip processing, packaging, and testing. Core technologies include PLC planar lightwave circuit technology, AWG chips for wavelength division multiplexing, DFB laser chips, and silicon photonics. They focus on advanced manufacturing processes such as co-packaged optics (CPO), high refractive index difference AWG chips, high-power continuous wave lasers for silicon photonics, and integrated photonic devices. Production methods include wafer-level processing, chip-level packaging, and module assembly with strict quality controls.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers include telecommunications operators, data center operators, optical module manufacturers, and system equipment vendors. The company serves domestic and international markets, with products widely used in telecom backbone and metro networks, fiber access networks (FTTH, FTTR), data centers supporting AI and cloud computing, 5G and upcoming 5.5G mobile networks, and emerging fields like lidar, satellite communications, and gas sensing. Major end markets are China and overseas regions including the US and Europe.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates primarily in China with headquarters and manufacturing facilities in Henan Province. It also has subsidiaries and operations in Shenzhen, Beijing, Wuhan, Wuxi, and an overseas subsidiary in California, USA. Overseas sales accounted for about 21.38% of total revenue in 2023, with active market development in North America and Europe. The company plans to expand international presence through overseas subsidiaries and global partnerships.
categories.supply_chain_position: Shijia Photons operates mainly in the upstream and midstream segments of the optical communications supply chain. It designs and manufactures core optical chips and devices (both passive and active), and produces optical cables and cable materials. The company’s IDM model integrates chip design, wafer fabrication, chip processing, packaging, and module assembly, positioning it as a key upstream supplier to optical module manufacturers and system integrators downstream.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company’s strategic focus is on continuous innovation in optical chip technologies, emphasizing both passive and active photonic devices. R&D priorities include high-speed data center interconnect chips (400G/800G/1.6T), silicon photonics, co-packaged optics, DWDM AWG chips, high-power DFB and EML lasers, and new application areas such as lidar, satellite communications, and gas sensing. The company invests heavily in R&D (12.73% of revenue in 2023), collaborates with leading research institutes like the Chinese Academy of Sciences, and pursues product integration and cost reduction to enhance competitiveness.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated through direct sales of optical chips, optical devices, indoor optical cables, and cable materials. The company employs a direct sales model supported by targeted marketing teams for domestic and international customers. Customized development services and product solutions are also offered, leveraging the company’s IDM capabilities. Revenue is recognized upon transfer of control to customers, typically at product shipment and acceptance.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: The company competes in the global optical communications industry dominated by players from the US, Japan, and China. It holds a strong domestic position as a leading manufacturer of PLC splitters, AWG chips, and DFB laser chips, with growing international recognition. The company benefits from high technical barriers in optical chip manufacturing and has achieved significant market penetration in data center and telecom applications. It faces competition from established global suppliers but is advancing through technology innovation and domestic market growth.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2023, the company reported revenue of approximately RMB 754.6 million, a 16.46% decline from 2022, with a net loss attributable to shareholders of RMB 47.5 million. Total assets stood at RMB 1.48 billion, and shareholders’ equity was RMB 1.13 billion. Despite short-term revenue and profit declines due to market and pricing pressures, the company maintains a robust R&D investment and a solid asset base. The company’s revenue and net profit have shown volatility, reflecting industry cyclicality and investment in innovation.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Shijia Photons emphasizes its IDM integrated manufacturing capability, enabling full control over chip design, fabrication, and packaging, which accelerates innovation and product customization. Its product differentiation lies in advanced photonic integration, high-performance optical chips (both passive and active), and tailored solutions for emerging high-speed data center and telecom networks. The company’s focus on silicon photonics, co-packaged optics, and diversified application fields like lidar and gas sensing provides competitive advantages. Its commitment to domestic production supports import substitution and supply chain security.
